summary: An administrator can forget a backup repository: Core drops its record, recovery-point list, run history, mounts and sealed credentials on the pool master and members, and never touches the destination.

guide.reason: Operators get the Forget workflow, its refusals, and the recovery path for a repository whose destination is gone or changed.

api.reason: New Controller route POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/backup-repositories/{repo_id}/forget, Core command backup-repository-forget, Core-local route POST /api/local/v1/pool/backup-repositories/{id}/forget and peer route POST /api/v1/pool/backup/forget. Administrator session, Origin and CSRF; the command is validated and receipted on the master, so a request_id replays its recorded outcome.

roadmap.reason: Completes the repository lifecycle inside the current backup slice; no milestone or acceptance gate changes.

state.record: pool-backup-repositories.json, pool-backup-catalog/, pool-backup-runs/ and the sealed backup credential receipts on the pool master; the same repository record, mount and credential on each member.
state.reason: Forgetting removes Core-owned state and the metadata receipt records the outcome; the Controller keeps only the operation row and adopts the smaller inventory from the master, so a fresh Controller sees the repository as gone.

verification.method: Focused Go tests in internal/agent (real master and member in the transfer lab, stubbed unmount) covering each refusal, success, member removal, replay, an already-forgotten repository, untouched destination data and credential retirement; a mutation of the pinned-point refusal made the test fail. Controller route test for CSRF, authentication, validation, queueing, replay and conflict. Web unit test and tsc. No browser walkthrough, real NFS/SMB/S3/SFTP destination, or multi-host lab was run.
